newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Romanian PM Ciorbea continues NATO-wooing exercise.
newsitem.headline: Romanian PM Ciorbea continues NATO-wooing exercise.

text.p: Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea continued on Monday his country's concerted efforts to woo support from NATO members for Bucharest's early entry into the western defence alliance.

Ciorbea, accompanied by Foreign Minister Adrian Severin and a sizeable delegation, met a series of ambassadors to the North Atlantic Treay Organisation to argue Romania's case for joining the first wave of entrants from former Soviet bloc countries.

"Many of the ambassadors were favourable... no one was against. There were only two or three who said that they had not yet taken their final decision as far as the first wave was concerned," Ciorbea told a news conference.
"Obviously there were ambassadors who declared without reticence their total support for the integration of Romania in the first wave," he added.
Ciorbea said the 16-nation alliance promised Romania a democratic bulwark for his country's newly elected government.
"It's a model of civilisation, it's a model of democracy to which we hold and to which we would like to belong," he added.
Diplomats said France, supported by the southern European NATO members, was backing Romania's application in the face of coolness from the United States, Britain and Germany.
A U.S. State Department spokesman said last week that Washington would not decide until May or June, ahead of the Madrid summit on NATO expansion in July, on whom to support.
Romania is among several countries jostling for early NATO membership along with acknowledged favourites Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic.
Bulgaria and Slovenia are also involved in eleventh-hour charm offensives, intent on first-wave membership.
